logs: idna::to_ascii: match (1230 probes) — `to_ascii(s)` returns the literal 4 bytes "xn--" concatenated with a byte-wise C-locale lowercased copy of s (only bytes 0x41..0x5A shift by +0x20; every other byte, including UTF-8 lead/continuation bytes and invalid UTF-8, passes through untouched). The prefix is added unconditionally with no ACE-prefix detection, no punycode transformation, no dot/label awareness, and no length limit, so to_ascii("") == "xn--" and to_ascii("XN--A") == "xn--xn--a"; it is locale-insensitive because the driver never calls setlocale.

idna::to_unicode: match (8426 probes) — to_unicode(s) removes a single leading literal ASCII "xn--" from the raw byte string s and returns the remainder, otherwise returns s verbatim: exactly `s.find("xn--") == 0 ? s.substr(4) : s` (confirmed at 0x40300a, needle literal at .rodata 0x406069). The match is byte-exact and case-sensitive ("XN--"/"Xn--"/"xN--" are left alone), anchored at offset 0 only (a prefix elsewhere in the string is never touched), and applied at most once ("xn--xn--a" -> "xn--a"); "xn--" alone yields the empty string, there is no UTF-8 decoding, no locale dependence, and no length limit or boundary of any kind.

punycode_encode: match (70621 probes) — `idna::punycode_encode(s)` performs no Punycode/Bootstring encoding at all: it unconditionally returns the byte string `"xn--" + s`, concatenating the 4-byte ACE literal onto the raw input bytes with no case folding, no length limit, and no check for an already-present `xn--` prefix (so `punycode_encode("xn--a")` is `"xn--xn--a"` and the empty input yields `"xn--"`). This differs from `to_ascii(s)`, which is `"xn--" + bytewise ::tolower(s)` — the two fields diverge on any input containing `A`-`Z` (e.g. `to_ascii("ExAmPlE.CoM")` = `xn--example.com` vs `punycode_encode("ExAmPlE.CoM")` = `xn--ExAmPlE.CoM`); confirmed in the disassembly, where `0x403071` only loads the `"xn--"` literal at `0x406069` and calls `std::operator+(char const*, std::string const&)`, while `to_ascii` at `0x402f5c` first runs `std::transform(..., tolower@plt)`.

idna::punycode_decode: match (11662 probes) — `punycode_decode(s)` does no punycode arithmetic: it returns `s.substr(4)` if and only if `s.find("xn--") == 0` (case-sensitive, prefix-anchored, byte-level, with no minimum-length guard so the 4-byte input "xn--" yields the empty string), and otherwise returns `s` byte-for-byte unchanged — including invalid UTF-8, dots, and arbitrarily long input. Its machine code at 0x40309c is instruction-identical to `to_unicode` at 0x40300a (same "xn--" literal at 0x406069, same `find(...)==0` test, same `substr(4, npos)`), so the two functions are indistinguishable on every possible input.

idna::is_valid_domain: match (5467 probes) — is_valid_domain(s) returns true if and only if the raw BYTE length of s lies in [1, 255] inclusive -- i.e. exactly `!s.empty() && s.length() <= 255` -- applying no character-class, dot/label-structure, per-label-63, ACE-prefix ("xn--"), UTF-8-validity, or case rules at all, and reading no library global state (set_strict_mode / set_verify_dns_length do not affect it). Because the bound counts bytes rather than code points, 85 three-byte CJK characters (255 bytes) is accepted while 86 (258 bytes) is rejected; the boundary was binary-searched to largest-valid=255 / smallest-invalid=256 and confirmed in the disassembly at 0x403103 as a std::string::empty() test followed by `cmp $0xff,%rax; ja`.

idna::is_valid_label: match (1422 probes) — is_valid_label(s) returns true iff the string is non-empty and its BYTE length is at most 63 — i.e. `!s.empty() && s.length() <= 63` applied to the WHOLE input string, never to dot-separated labels, with no character-class rules at all (dots, hyphens, underscores, spaces, control bytes, and invalid UTF-8 are all accepted as ordinary bytes). Confirmed in the disassembly at 0x403144: `call empty; xor $0x1; je fail; call length; cmp $0x3f,%rax; ja fail; mov $1`.

idna::is_ascii_domain: match (205917 probes) — `is_ascii_domain(s)` walks the whole std::string byte-by-byte and returns false on the first byte that is negative as a signed char (any byte >= 0x80), else true; it applies no length cap, no dot/label rules and no "xn--" special-casing, so the empty string is vacuously true (field 7 = 1), 0x00-0x7f are accepted and 0x80-0xff rejected regardless of position. Confirmed at 0x403183 where the loop body is `movzbl (%rax),%eax; mov %al,-0x9(%rbp); cmpb $0x0,-0x9(%rbp); jns continue` with `mov $0x0,%eax` on fallthrough and `mov $0x1,%eax` at loop exit - a signed sign test against 0, not a literal 0x80 compare; field 8 (is_idn_domain) is its exact negation (`xor $0x1,%eax`).

idna::is_idn_domain: match (5039 probes) — `is_idn_domain(s)` returns exactly `!is_ascii_domain(s)`, where `is_ascii_domain(s)` is true iff every byte of `s` has its high bit clear (`(signed char)c >= 0`, i.e. byte < 0x80), with the empty string vacuously ASCII; so field 8 is 1 iff `s` contains at least one byte in 0x80..0xFF and 0 otherwise, with no dependence on length, dot placement, `xn--` prefixes, or UTF-8 validity. The disassembly confirms it literally as `call is_ascii_domain; xor $0x1,%eax`, and since `is_ascii_domain` only ever returns literal 0 or 1, field 8 is a provably exact negation of field 7 for every possible input.

idna::to_lower: match (1071 probes) — to_lower returns a copy of the input with std::transform(..., ::tolower) applied byte-by-byte in the process's default "C" locale (main never calls setlocale), so it is strictly ASCII case folding: bytes 0x41-0x5A are shifted to 0x61-0x7A and every other byte 0x01-0x40 / 0x5B-0xFF — including all UTF-8 lead and continuation bytes, raw Latin-1 high bytes, dots, and invalid UTF-8 — is returned unchanged, preserving length exactly; it has no UTF-8/locale awareness (Turkish dotted I, Greek, and accented Latin-1 are untouched, and LC_ALL/LANG/LC_CTYPE have no effect) and no label/length limits. idna::normalize is a pure forwarder to to_lower, so field 10 is always byte-identical to field 9.

idna::normalize: match (1270 probes) — idna::normalize(s) is a pure forwarding thunk to idna::to_lower(s) (disassembly at 0x403490 tail-calls 0x403404 with the sret pointer and argument unchanged), and to_lower is std::transform(begin,end,begin,::tolower) with each char sign-extended to int and only the low result byte stored back; since the binary never calls setlocale, the "C" locale applies and exactly the bytes 0x41-0x5A ('A'-'Z') are shifted by +32 while every other byte — including UTF-8 continuation bytes, invalid UTF-8, whitespace, and dots — passes through verbatim, with no Unicode/NFC/NFD normalization, no whitespace trimming, no trailing-dot stripping, and no length truncation. Therefore field 10 is byte-for-byte identical to field 9 for every possible input and can never differ from it.

idna::count_labels: match (9855 probes) — count_labels(s) returns exactly (number of raw 0x2E '.' bytes in s) + 1, with no special cases at all: the empty string yields 1, "." yields 2, ".." yields 3, and leading, trailing, and consecutive empty labels are each counted individually (".a." -> 3, "a..b" -> 3). Matching is purely byte-wise on 0x2E, so multi-byte dot look-alikes (U+3002, U+FF0E) and the overlong encoding \xc0\xae contribute nothing while a bare 0x2E inside invalid UTF-8 does count; there is no length clamping or cap, and the int counter cannot overflow because a single argv entry is limited to 131071 bytes.
